Fees for brain injury attorneys in pedestrian accidents?


The aftermath of a pedestrian accident can be overwhelming, especially when a brain injury is involved. Beyond the immediate pain and recovery, you likely face a mountain of medical bills and lost income. It is natural to wonder about the costs associated with securing the legal help you need. At Silberstein & Miklos, P.C., we believe in absolute transparency regarding Fees for brain injury attorneys in pedestrian accidents? Our mission is to ensure you understand every aspect of how legal representation works, so you can focus on healing without added financial stress.
Key TakeawaysPedestrian accident victims dealing with brain injuries deserve clear information about how attorney fees work before committing to legal representation.Most brain injury attorneys operate on a contingency fee basis, meaning clients pay nothing upfront and legal costs are collected only if compensation is recovered.Silberstein & Miklos, P.C. prioritizes full transparency so that injured pedestrians can concentrate on medical recovery rather than worrying about hidden legal expenses.Understanding the fee structure empowers accident victims to make confident decisions about pursuing fair compensation for medical bills and lost wages.

Table of ContentsHow Brain Injury Attorney Fees Work in Pedestrian Accident CasesBreaking Down Every Cost: From Free Consultation to Final SettlementReal Settlement Fee Examples: What You Actually Take HomeQuestions to Ask Any Brain Injury Attorney About Fees Before SigningWhy Trial-Ready Representation Commands Better Settlements


We know that the insurance companies are not on your side. They aim to minimize payouts, and navigating their tactics alone is a daunting task. That is where our experienced legal team steps in. We are committed to fighting for maximum compensation for victims of negligence. Understanding our fee structure is the first step in partnering with a firm dedicated to your justice. Rest assured, our primary concern is securing the best possible outcome for you, and our fee arrangement is designed to reflect that commitment.
Learn More

How Brain Injury Attorney Fees Work in Pedestrian Accident Cases

What Is a Contingency Fee Agreement? Plain-English Explanation

The cornerstone of personal injury representation, particularly for complex cases like pedestrian accidents involving brain injuries, is the contingency fee agreement. This arrangement means our firm only gets paid if we successfully recover compensation for you, whether through a settlement or a trial verdict. Your attorney's fees are contingent upon winning your case. This structure ensures that your financial situation does not prevent you from accessing top-tier legal advocacy. We invest our time, resources, and expertise into your claim, aligning our success directly with yours.

With a contingency fee, you do not pay any hourly rates or upfront retainers. The firm advances all costs associated with litigating your case. If we do not secure a settlement or win a verdict on your behalf, you owe us nothing for our legal services. This "no win, no fee" promise is fundamental to how we operate, providing you with peace of mind and the assurance that your legal team is fully committed to achieving the best possible outcome for your pedestrian accident claim.

Typical Fee Percentages for Brain Injury Cases in New York

In New York, personal injury attorneys typically work on a contingency fee basis, with percentages generally ranging from 33% to 40% of the final recovery. This percentage is agreed upon at the outset of the representation. As an AV-rated firm, Silberstein & Miklos, P.C. stands by this transparent model. We understand that brain injury cases can be particularly costly due to extensive medical needs and expert testimony, and our fee structure is designed to ensure you receive the maximum net recovery possible. We are committed to providing exceptional value for our services.

The specific percentage can sometimes depend on the complexity of the case and whether it proceeds to trial. Nevertheless, our commitment remains unwavering: to provide aggressive, high-quality representation. We are proud to offer services throughout New York City boroughs and surrounding areas, including Bronx, Brooklyn, Manhattan, Queens, and Long Island. For those injured in Long Island, our Long Island Personal Injury Lawyers are ready to assist with the same dedication and expertise.



Attorney Fees If Your Case Does Not Win

A common concern for individuals facing the aftermath of a pedestrian accident is the financial risk if their case is unsuccessful. With a contingency fee agreement, this worry is eliminated. If Silberstein & Miklos, P.C. does not achieve a settlement or win a verdict for your brain injury claim, you will not owe us any legal fees for our services. We cover all the expenses associated with litigating your case, including filing fees, expert witness costs, and more. Our firm's investment in your case means you can pursue justice without the burden of upfront costs or paying attorney fees if there is no recovery.



Breaking Down Every Cost: From Free Consultation to Final Settlement

  


The Free Initial Consultation. What to Expect at Silberstein & Miklos

Your journey toward recovery and justice begins with a completely free, no-obligation initial consultation at Silberstein & Miklos, P.C. This is your opportunity to discuss the specifics of your pedestrian accident, understand your legal options, and ask any questions you may have about fees and the legal process. Our attorneys will listen compassionately, assess the details of your case, and explain how we can help. We also use this time to detail our contingency fee structure, ensuring you have a clear picture of costs from the very start. There are no hidden fees or surprises; our goal is to provide you with the information and reassurance you need.

During this consultation, we will begin to gather information about the incident, your injuries, and the impact it has had on your life. This initial meeting is essential for us to understand the scope of your claim and for you to feel confident in our ability to represent you. We encourage you to bring any relevant documents you may have, such as police reports or medical records, though they are not required for this first discussion. Our team is ready to guide you through this essential first step, offering clarity and support.

Case Expenses vs. Attorney Fees: Expert Witnesses, Filing Fees, Medical Records

It is essential to distinguish between attorney fees and case expenses. While attorney fees are contingent on a successful outcome, case expenses are the costs incurred to build and prosecute your claim. These can include obtaining medical records, police reports, court filing fees, deposition costs, and, importantly for brain injury cases, fees for expert witnesses such as medical specialists, accident reconstructionists, and economists. These experts are often essential in proving the extent of your injuries and damages, especially for a traumatic brain injury.

At Silberstein & Miklos, P.C., we advance these necessary case expenses on your behalf. This means you do not have to pay for these significant costs out-of-pocket as your case develops. We absorb the financial risk, allowing us to pursue the strongest possible claim for you. This practice is standard for reputable personal injury firms, especially those like ours serving clients in Long Island, where our Long Island Personal Injury Lawyers are equipped to handle complex litigation. The firm's commitment to covering these costs upfront underscores our dedication to securing maximum compensation for you.



How Case Expenses Are Reimbursed From Your Settlement

Once your case is successfully resolved, either through a settlement or a trial verdict, the agreed-upon attorney fees and all advanced case expenses are reimbursed. The order of these deductions is typically outlined in your retainer agreement. The settlement funds are first applied to reimburse the firm for any case expenses that were advanced. Following the reimbursement of expenses, the attorney's contingency fee is calculated based on the remaining amount. This ensures that the firm's costs are covered before the net recovery is disbursed to you. We maintain meticulous records of all expenses, providing full transparency on how your settlement is allocated.





Real Settlement Fee Examples: What You Actually Take Home

Sample Fee Breakdown at Different Settlement Amounts

Understanding Fees for brain injury attorneys in pedestrian accidents? requires more than knowing percentages. It demands clarity on how those fees impact your final recovery. Let’s review concrete examples at three settlement levels: $100,000, $250,000, and $500,000. These figures reflect typical outcomes in New York pedestrian brain injury cases, where settlements vary depending on injury severity and liability strength.

At a $100,000 settlement, assuming a 33.3% contingency fee, the attorney’s share would be approximately $33,333. From the remaining $66,667, case expenses such as expert witness fees and filing costs. Often ranging from $5,000 to $20,000 in brain injury cases. Are reimbursed. For illustration, if expenses total $10,000, the net amount to the client becomes roughly $56,667. This example highlights the impact of necessary litigation costs, which attorneys like Silberstein & Miklos, P.C. advance upfront to avoid financial strain on clients.

For a $250,000 settlement, the attorney’s fee calculated at 33.3% equals about $83,333. Deducting $15,000 in case expenses, the remaining client net is approximately $151,667. Larger settlements typically involve proportionally higher expenses due to more extensive medical documentation and expert analysis. Our firm’s transparent approach ensures clients understand these deductions before agreeing to representation.

At the $500,000 level, the contingency fee may be subject to New York’s sliding scale rules, explained further below. Without adjusting the fee, 33.3% would be $166,667. After reimbursing $20,000 in expenses, the client would receive $313,333. The scale aims to balance fair compensation for legal services with maximizing client recovery, especially in high-value cases.

How New York's Sliding Scale Fee Structure Works for Larger Settlements

New York Judiciary Law Section 474-a governs contingency fees in personal injury cases, including brain injury claims from pedestrian accidents. This statute establishes a sliding scale fee structure to prevent excessive attorney fees in large settlements or verdicts. The sliding scale applies when recoveries exceed $250,000, adjusting the percentage taken as the total amount increases.

Specifically, the sliding scale caps fees as follows: 33.3% on the first $250,000, 30% on the next $250,000, and 25% on any amount exceeding $500,000. This means for a $500,000 recovery, the attorney fee would be $83,333 (33.3% of the first $250,000) plus $75,000 (30% of the next $250,000), totaling $158,333. Slightly less than the flat 33.3% calculation. For settlements above $500,000, the portion exceeding that amount is charged at 25%, reducing the overall fee percentage and increasing the client’s net recovery.

This sliding scale provision reflects New York’s commitment to fair attorney compensation while protecting injured clients from disproportionate fees. It benefits clients by increasing their net settlement as amounts grow, which is particularly important in complex brain injury cases where damages can reach into the millions. Silberstein & Miklos, P.C. adheres strictly to these guidelines and educates clients on how fees are calculated to maintain transparency and trust.

Clients in Long Island and surrounding areas should know that our Long Island Personal Injury Lawyers specialize in navigating these fee structures. We ensure clients receive the maximum possible net compensation while handling all case expenses upfront, including expert witness fees, filing charges, and medical record costs. Our team’s extensive trial experience helps maximize settlements, making the fee percentage a smaller portion of a larger recovery.



Questions to Ask Any Brain Injury Attorney About Fees Before Signing

When you've suffered a brain injury in a pedestrian accident, the legal process can seem daunting, especially when considering attorney fees. It is paramount that you approach any potential representation with a clear understanding of costs. Asking the right questions upfront ensures transparency and helps you make an informed decision. This is not just about finding someone to take your case; it’s about partnering with a legal team whose fee structure aligns with your best interests and whose value is evident in their commitment to your recovery and compensation. Our firm believes in equipping clients with knowledge, so you can confidently move forward.

The aftermath of a pedestrian accident, particularly one involving a brain injury, is a time of immense stress. Insurance companies may try to take advantage of your vulnerability, making it essential to have a seasoned legal advocate. Before signing any agreement, you must fully grasp how Fees for brain injury attorneys in pedestrian accidents? are determined and what your financial obligations will be. This diligence protects you from unexpected charges and ensures you are working with a firm that prioritizes your net recovery. We encourage you to be thorough. Your peace of mind during this challenging period is as important as the outcome of your case.

The Essential Fee-Transparency Checklist

To ensure you have a complete picture, use this checklist when discussing fees with any potential brain injury attorney for your pedestrian accident claim. First, confirm the contingency fee percentage and understand if it applies to the gross settlement or the net amount after expenses. Clarify what constitutes "case expenses". This includes court costs, expert witness fees, medical record retrieval, and investigative costs. You must know who covers these expenses initially and how they are reimbursed from the settlement. Ask if the firm advances these costs, as this is a significant indicator of their commitment and financial capacity to fight for you. Also, inquire about the specific percentage applied if the case goes to trial, as some agreements may differ.

Additionally, ask how the firm handles situations where a case is settled versus won at trial; sometimes, the fee structure can vary. Understand the process for obtaining an accounting of all fees and expenses at the conclusion of the case. It is also wise to ask if the firm has specific fee arrangements for different types of recoveries, such as structured settlements versus lump-sum payouts. A truly transparent agreement will be detailed and easy to understand, leaving no room for ambiguity. Remember, clarity now prevents complications later. For residents of Long Island, our Long Island Personal Injury Lawyers are committed to this level of upfront honesty.

Warning Signs That a Fee Agreement May Not Be in Your Favor

Be vigilant for certain red flags in fee agreements. Any reluctance from an attorney to clearly explain their fee structure or case expenses is a significant warning sign. If an agreement seems vague, uses confusing legal jargon without proper explanation, or feels rushed, proceed with extreme caution. A firm that pressures you to sign immediately, without allowing ample time for review and questions, may not have your best interests at heart. Another concern is a fee percentage that seems unusually low or excessively high compared to industry standards, as it might signal a lack of experience or an attempt to obscure the total cost.





Pros of Clear Fee Agreements



Builds trust and confidence between client and firm.

Ensures client protection from unexpected costs.

Facilitates informed decision-making regarding legal representation.

Aligns attorney and client goals for maximum recovery.

Demonstrates firm's commitment to ethical practices.







Cons of Vague or Overtly Complex Fee Agreements



Can lead to disputes and dissatisfaction later.

May hide additional charges or unfavorable terms.

Indicates a potential lack of transparency or respect for the client.

Could result in a lower net recovery for the client.

May signal inexperience or a focus on firm profit over client justice.







Why the Lowest Percentage Does Not Always Mean the Best Outcome

It is tempting to seek out the attorney offering the lowest contingency fee percentage, but this approach can be shortsighted. The percentage is only one part of the equation; the total net recovery you receive is what truly matters. A highly experienced, trial-ready firm might charge a standard or slightly higher percentage, but their ability to secure a significantly larger settlement or verdict can result in you taking home more money overall. For example, a firm with a strong track record in brain injury litigation might achieve a $2 million settlement, while a less experienced firm might only secure $1 million, even with a lower percentage fee on the smaller amount.

The true value of an attorney lies in their skill, resources, and tenacity. Brain injury cases are complex and often require extensive investigation, expert testimony, and aggressive negotiation or litigation. A firm that is prepared to go the distance, backed by decades of courtroom experience like Silberstein & Miklos, P.C., is better positioned to maximize your compensation. When considering fees for brain injury attorneys in pedestrian accidents, evaluate the firm's reputation, their history of success in similar cases, and their commitment to trial readiness. These factors are often more indicative of a favorable outcome than a lower fee percentage alone.




Why Trial-Ready Representation Commands Better Settlements

  


In the complex arena of personal injury law, particularly for severe injuries like those resulting from pedestrian accidents involving brain trauma, the willingness and ability of your legal team to go to trial is a powerful negotiating tool. Insurance companies know which firms are prepared to fight aggressively in court. This reputation for trial readiness directly influences their approach to settlement negotiations. A firm that consistently demonstrates its capability to win in front of a judge and jury compels insurers to offer more favorable terms to avoid the risk and expense of a trial. This readiness is not just a promise; it's a strategic advantage that can significantly increase your net recovery.

At Silberstein & Miklos, P.C., our attorneys are not just negotiators; we are seasoned litigators. This dual expertise means we are equipped to handle every stage of your claim, from initial investigation and settlement discussions to preparing for and conducting a full trial. Our AV-rated status reflects not only our legal knowledge and ethical standards but also our proven success in the courtroom. This level of distinction reassures clients that their case is being handled by professionals who command respect from opposing counsel and the courts. The Fees for brain injury attorneys in pedestrian accidents? are justified by this capacity to secure the best possible results, whether through settlement or verdict.

How AV-Rated Experience Directly Impacts Your Net Recovery

The Martindale-Hubbell AV rating is the highest possible peer review rating for attorneys, signifying preeminent legal ability and ethical standards. For clients seeking representation in complex brain injury cases stemming from pedestrian accidents, this rating is a critical indicator of a firm's qualifications. An AV-rated firm, such as Silberstein & Miklos, P.C., possesses the deep legal knowledge, extensive trial experience, and unwavering ethical commitment necessary to navigate sophisticated legal challenges. This experience translates directly into a higher likelihood of achieving a more substantial settlement or verdict.

Our firm's decades of courtroom dominance mean we understand how to effectively present evidence, cross-examine witnesses, and construct compelling arguments that align with judges and juries. This expertise is invaluable when dealing with insurance adjusters who may initially undervalue your claim. The confidence and authority that come with an AV rating allow our attorneys to negotiate from a position of strength. This often results in settlements that reflect the true value of your damages, including medical expenses, lost wages, pain, and suffering, ultimately leading to a greater net recovery for you and your family. We are dedicated to securing justice and maximum compensation for every client.

Next Steps: Call Our Consultation Hotline Before Evidence Fades

The critical window for preserving essential evidence in a pedestrian accident case, especially one involving a brain injury, is often short. Memories fade, accident scenes change, and essential documentation can be lost or altered. Prompt action is essential to build the strongest possible case. So, we urge you to contact Silberstein & Miklos, P.C. immediately to schedule your free, no-obligation consultation. Our dedicated legal team is ready to listen, assess your situation, and explain how we can fight for your rights.

Learn More
Do not delay in seeking the legal guidance you deserve. The sooner you connect with us, the sooner we can begin the work necessary to protect your interests and pursue the compensation to which you are entitled. Call our consultation hotline today. Let us carry the legal burden so you can focus on healing and recovery. We are here to provide the commanding, compassionate, and effective representation that accident victims need.
